title_en: Amazon revises its terms and conditions... Consumer class action restrictions
summary_en: [ZD Net Korea] Amazon has reintroduced a clause in its terms of use that restricts consumers from filing class action lawsuits. This is a measure to reduce the legal burden of class action lawsuits by resolving disputes through arbitration procedures rather than in court. According to Bloomberg News on the 15th (local time), Amazon sent an email to customers on the 14th and announced that it would add an ‘arbitration agreement and class action waiver clause’ to its terms of use. Under the new terms, if a dispute arises with Amazon, consumers must resolve it through arbitration instead of filing a lawsuit in court. Class action lawsuits involving multiple consumers are also restricted. However, claims can be filed in small claims court, where damages are usually limited to a few thousand dollars. An Amazon spokesperson said, “We are continuously improving our Terms of Use to provide better service to our customers. Reintroducing the arbitration clause allows customers to quickly and cost-effectively resolve disputes while also maintaining the right to choose small claims court.” Amazon previously removed a similar arbitration clause from its 2021 Terms of Use. At the time, as legal disputes surrounding personal information protection issues with the voice recognition device ‘Alexa’ ensued, the terms and conditions were changed. Afterwards, Amazon continued to address safety issues with products sold on the platform and the cancellation of Prime membership, a paid subscription service…
